subject: ventures/survival-analysis
professional: a senior biostatistician who reports time-to-event endpoints in clinical papers. They would check first that the Kaplan-Meier estimate and Greenwood SE match a textbook table, that the log-rank statistic on the 6-MP data is 16.79, that the Cox fit with Breslow and Efron ties reproduces published coefficients and -2 log L, that the median CI follows Brookmeyer-Crowley on the chosen band scale, that the PH test is the Grambsch-Therneau one, and whether a KM figure comes with a number-at-risk table

evidence.correctness: Ran the CLI on the bundled Freireich 6-MP data and checked against sources the author did not write. (a) Kaplan-Meier for 6-MP: S = 0.8571/0.8067/0.7529/0.6902/0.6275/0.5378/0.4482 at t = 6,7,10,13,16,22,23 with Greenwood SE 0.0764/0.0869/0.0963/0.1068/0.1141/0.1282/0.1346, identical to the textbook table (Klein & Moeschberger, Survival Analysis, 2nd ed., Table 4.1A); median 23 weeks, placebo 8. (b) Log-rank 16.793 on 1 df, O/E 9/19.25 and 21/10.75, the published value (Kleinbaum & Klein 2012, ch. 2: 16.79). (c) Breslow-ties Cox, Rx only: coef 1.509 se 0.410 HR 4.523, -2LL 172.759 vs null 187.970; Rx + logWBC: 1.294 (HR 3.648) and 1.604 (HR 4.975), -2LL 144.559: all four numbers equal Kleinbaum & Klein's Stata output (ch. 3, Models 1 and 2). Efron coef 1.572 se 0.412, LR 16.35, Wald 14.53, score 17.25 equal R coxph on the same data as widely reproduced (Therneau). (d) On a new seeded data set the author never used (300 rows, 4 arms, integer months with heavy ties, age and a 3-level text covariate; scratchpad indep.py): own numpy KM and Greenwood max diff 0; own hand k-sample log-rank 35.763282785826 vs engine ...611 vs lifelines ...609; Gehan-Breslow and Tarone-Ware vs statsmodels survdiff to 1e-14; medians and both CI ends equal lifelines for all 4 arms; Cox coefficients and SEs vs statsmodels PHReg to 2e-15 for Efron and Breslow, log-lik equal; LR 83.2875 vs lifelines; Harrell C 0.66933718 identical; Grambsch-Therneau p (km transform) vs lifelines to 3e-6. (e) Re-ran the author's eval/reference.py in a scratch copy: every number in reference.json identical (max abs diff 0). Not 4-limiting: the median at a flat S = 0.5 takes the first time (R takes the midpoint), and >~130k rows throw a RangeError (craft).
evidence.completeness: README/page claims checked end to end via CLI and engine: KM with log(-log) bands and censoring ticks (chart code read, page.test.mjs exercises the script), median + CI, RMST with --tau, log-rank / Gehan-Breslow / Tarone-Ware, k groups, --reference, Cox Efron/Breslow with LR/Wald/score, per-term PH test, Harrell C, text covariates dummy-coded, event coding (1/0, yes/no, 1/2 as R, --event-value), missing rows dropped and counted, --json, stdin, CSV download (code read), agent call documented. All worked. Gaps: the served page https://marisstella.app/survival-analysis/ could not be loaded (proxy CONNECT 403), so the page was checked through page.test.mjs and source only; no number-at-risk table, no figure export. No TODOs or stubs. 3.
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/survival-analysis && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 44 tests, 44 pass, 0.45 s. Tests pin KM (1e-12), bands (1e-9), log-rank (1e-10), Cox coef/SE/loglik (1e-8..1e-10) against lifelines and statsmodels on 4 data sets, plus identities (score test = log-rank with no ties) and properties. Seeded 12 mutations in engine.mjs, each reverted with git checkout: Greenwood term, log-rank variance (N-D)/(N-1)->N/N, covariance -nRisk/N -> /(N+1), Gehan weight n -> n-1, Efron f -> 0 (Breslow), median <= -> <, concordance censored-at-t insertion removed, PH transform 1-KM(t) -> t, separation threshold 12 -> 1200: all 9 caught. Survived: RMST break `>=` -> `>` (an equivalent mutant), the RMST-beyond-follow-up warning disabled (engine.mjs:612) and the single-group warning disabled (engine.mjs:594): two user-facing warnings untested. The reference generator reproduces bit for bit. 4.
evidence.craft: Read engine.mjs (677 lines), cli.mjs, index.html script, usage.mjs, all four test files, eval/reference.py. Clean pure-function engine, one O(n log n) concordance with a Fenwick tree, step-halving Newton with convergence and separation warnings, careful event coding and readable errors. Defects: `Math.max(...eta)` (engine.mjs:359) and `Math.max(...tg)` (engine.mjs:604) spread the whole column onto the call stack; at 150,000 rows analyze() throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` (120,000 works), and the page's runAnalysis (index.html:313) has no try/catch, so the Analyze button silently does nothing. Event values `1.0/0.0` (pandas/Excel exports) are rejected (engine.mjs:138-157). 3.
evidence.claims: Checked: '16.79 on 1 df (p = 4.2e-5)', 'median 23 (13 to not reached)', 'placebo 8 (4 to 11)', RMST 17.9/8.67, 'HR 4.82 (2.15 to 10.8), LR 16.35, Wald 14.53, score 17.25', 'Breslow 1.509', 'logWBC: 4.00 (1.74 to 9.20), 5.42', 'sex PH p = 0.052' (README:38-48): all reproduced by the CLI. 'checked against lifelines and statsmodels' (README, llms.txt, page meta): backed by eval/reference.json, reproduced by re-running eval/reference.py, and by my own new-data comparison. 'nothing uploaded / no analytics vendors' (index.html:202): usage.mjs only writes localStorage, page.test.mjs asserts no network calls. 'Not checked against R' and the log(-log) band / approximate PH-test departures are disclosed (README:85-90). Data provenance and SHA in data/SOURCE.md. Disclaimer on page, README, llms.txt, CLI. Unbacked or undisclosed: the median convention differs from R at a flat S = 0.5 (page says 'first time at or below 0.5' but not that R differs); the live page could not be fetched from this session. 3.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: a biostatistician pastes a 2-arm trial CSV, gets KM curves with bands, medians with CI, log-rank, a Cox HR adjusted for a covariate with PH check: every number matched a reference tool, so for a quick look, teaching or a churn/reliability analyst it does the job. For a paper they would still reach for R: no number-at-risk table under the curve (standard in published KM figures), no survival-at-time-t with CI in the summary (only in the downloadable table), no choice of reference level for text covariates (first seen is used, e.g. 'stage=I vs III'), no strata (open PR #14929 adds stratified Cox; not on main), no global PH test, no figure export. Stated limits are honest. 3.
evidence.domain: Compared with R survival / Stata / Kalbfleisch-Prentice practice: product-limit and Greenwood are standard; log(-log) bands match Stata's default (R defaults to log, disclosed); median CI by band crossing (Brookmeyer-Crowley style) matches lifelines; log-rank with hypergeometric covariance, Fleming-Harrington-free weighted tests; Cox with Efron/Breslow, three global tests, Harrell C with tied-time handling equal to lifelines. Departures a biostatistician would note: the PH test is the approximate (lifelines) Grambsch-Therneau statistic without a GLOBAL test (R cox.zph >= 3.0 is exact; disclosed); median at an exact 0.5 plateau takes the left end rather than R's midpoint; text-covariate reference not selectable; events-per-variable warning is the 10-EPV rule of thumb (fine). Would sign off on the methods within the stated limits. 3.

verdict: Expert-grade numerics: on data the author never used, Kaplan-Meier, Greenwood, k-sample log-rank, Gehan-Breslow, Tarone-Ware, Cox (Efron and Breslow), Harrell's C and the Grambsch-Therneau test agree with my own numpy code, lifelines and statsmodels to 1e-14 or better, and the 6-MP outputs equal the published textbook values (Klein & Moeschberger Table 4.1A; Kleinbaum & Klein log-rank 16.79 and Breslow Cox Models 1 and 2 including -2 log L). The author's reference generator reproduces bit for bit and 9 of 9 non-trivial core mutations are caught. It meets the bar (correctness 4, verification 4, claims 3, median 3). What keeps fitness and domain at 3: a crash above ~130k rows that the page swallows silently, no number-at-risk table, no choice of reference level for text covariates, no strata on main, and an undisclosed median convention difference from R.
